description: A bank of up to eight oscillators tuned to one pitch, then detuned against each other and modulated by filtered noise, summed to a single sawtooth and a single sine.

params.text: Sets the pitch in semitones, 8 octaves from -48 to +48; 0 gives C4 at 261.63Hz.
Sets the pitch over one semitone either side of COARSE, despite the manual giving about half an octave.
Attenuates the FM input, from nothing at 0 to a quarter of an octave per volt at 10.
Detunes the oscillators either side of the centre pitch; the amount is the cube of the setting, so it stays small for most of the travel and reaches 21 semitones at the top.
Sets how deep the filtered noise pushes each oscillator's pitch around; the depth is the cube of the setting, and at 10 the wandering runs to several octaves.
Sets the corner of the lowpass on that noise, and so how fast the wandering is, from 0.1Hz rising as the sixth power of the setting; it is continuous, not the six steps of the manual.
Chooses how many oscillators run, 2, 4 or 8; the sum is divided by that number, so the level stays the same, despite the manual saying a setting of 2 is louder.

inputs.text: Sets the pitch of every oscillator together, 1V/octave, added to COARSE and FINE; the number of channels patched here is the module's polyphony.
Modulates the pitch of every oscillator, through the FM knob, which at 10 gives a quarter of an octave per volt.
Hard-syncs every oscillator, resetting the phases on each upward crossing of 0V, rather than at the +0.25V threshold the manual gives.
Adds to the SPREAD knob, a tenth of its travel per volt, with the total held between 0 and 10.
Adds to the CHAOS knob, a tenth of its travel per volt, with the total held between 0 and 10.
Adds to the CHAOS BW knob, a tenth of its travel per volt, with the total held between 0 and 10.

outputs.text: The sawtooth waves of every running oscillator, summed and divided by their number, ±5V, through a 20Hz high-pass that removes the offset.
The sine waves of every running oscillator, summed and divided by their number, ±5V, through a 20Hz high-pass that removes the offset.

notes: There are no attenuators on the CV inputs. A ±5V signal reaches the whole of a control's range only with that control's knob at its midpoint, because the total is clamped.
The module is polyphonic. Every polyphonic channel runs its own bank of oscillators with its own noise, so a chord comes out as a chord of clouds rather than one.
The oscillators are stopped altogether while both output jacks are empty, and restart from wherever their phases were left.
menu: Spread tuning: Fourths, Fifths — chooses the intervals the detuned oscillators are spread across; Initialize puts it back to Fourths.
